world: Old rural Norway, in a deep mountain valley. Gudbrand's small farm lies high up on a steep hillside, and a narrow path zigzags down past the neighbour's farm to the valley road and a small market town far below. Inside the cottage is one warm room with a fireplace, a long table with benches, a painted cupboard and a big wooden chest. Gudbrand and his wife have three children: a boy of about twelve with short black hair and a green jumper, a girl of about nine with two stubby fair plaits and a red dress, and a small boy of about six in a long white shirt. The animals: a black cow with a white face, a sandy-yellow fjord horse with a striped pale mane, a fat pink pig, a white nanny goat, a woolly white sheep, a big white goose and a cinnamon-brown rooster.
palette: A warm, dusty late-September day in the valley: hazy golden air, yellowing birches, rowans heavy with red berries, grey dust on the road and on everything along it, low amber sun and long violet shadows in the afternoon. Then a clear, cool night with a big orange harvest moon over the mountains. Inside the cottage: warm firelight and candlelight on honey-brown timber. Accents: the wife’s cornflower-blue apron and rowan red.

cast.look: A short, round, easy-going farmer of about sixty with a round belly, a shiny bald head, fluffy white side-whiskers from his ears down to his jaw, a clean-shaven chin, a big pink nose, small merry blue eyes and a calm, contented smile. He wears a soft dark-green felt hat with a narrow brim, a thick knitted jacket with a black-and-white snowflake pattern and pewter clasps, brown breeches, grey wool stockings and heavy boots, and always has a short curved wooden pipe.
cast.portrait: Background: the steep hillside path with the valley far below.

simplified.name: Gudbrand i Lien
simplified.description: En rolig og godtroende bonde som stadig bytter til det han tror er noe bedre, og som stoler fullt og helt på at kona vil forstå ham.

english.name: Gudbrand-on-the-Slope
english.description: A well-meaning farmer who cheerfully trades his way home and trusts that his wife will see the good in it.

cast.look: A plump, cheerful farm wife of about fifty, a little shorter than Gudbrand, with a round, beaming face, rosy cheeks, a broad, freckled nose, merry hazel eyes that crinkle when she laughs and grey hair pinned up in a neat bun. She wears a long rose-red wool dress with a white linen collar and rolled-up sleeves, a bright cornflower-blue apron tied with a big bow at the back, and a cream knitted shawl round her shoulders.
cast.portrait: Background: the warm, firelit Cottage Room.

simplified.name: Kona
simplified.description: Gudbrands usedvanlig støttende kone som alltid finner en god grunn til å være fornøyd, uansett hva han har gjort.

english.name: Gudbrand’s Wife
english.description: Practical and remarkably supportive, she praises each decision and turns every loss into a blessing.

cast.look: A nosy, pot-bellied farmer of about fifty with a round, clean-shaven face, a long, pointed, twitchy nose, narrow doubtful eyes with one eyebrow always raised, big pink ears that stick straight out and short, spiky ginger hair. He wears a patched mustard-brown wool jacket with a sheepskin collar, a round brown felt hat, grey breeches and tall, scuffed boots.

simplified.name: Nabomannen
simplified.description: En skeptisk nabo som tror Gudbrand vil få kjeft hjemme, og som ender med å tape veddemålet.

english.name: The Neighbor
english.description: A skeptical local farmer who wagers that Gudbrand’s wife will finally scold him—and listens outside the door to find out.

places.name: the Hillside Farm
places.look: A tiny farm high on a steep hillside: a low, dark-brown log cottage with a thick turf roof growing grass and wild flowers, a stone chimney, two small four-paned windows and a sturdy plank door painted dusky blue, with a little cowshed beside it. A birch and a rowan tree heavy with red berries stand in the yard, and a narrow path zigzags steeply down towards the valley and a small town far below.

places.name: the Cottage Room
places.look: A snug, low-ceilinged log room with honey-brown timber walls. In one corner a whitewashed stone fireplace holds a crackling fire and a black iron pot. A long, scrubbed plank table with two benches stands under a small four-paned window, beside a big wooden chest with iron bands. There is a tall cupboard painted with red-and-blue rosemaling, a shelf of wooden bowls, pegs with coats and hats, and a dusky-blue plank door with an iron latch.

cover.prompt: Gudbrand strolls happily along a dusty valley road in the golden late-afternoon light, a cinnamon-brown rooster tucked under one arm and his pipe in the corner of his mouth, looking as pleased as a man who has made the best bargain in the world. Far up on the steep hillside above him, the Hillside Farm waits in the sun among yellow birches.

simplified.caption: Det er alltid bedre å ha hane enn gås, tenkte Gudbrand.
simplified.alt: Gudbrand rusler fornøyd langs en støvete vei med en brun hane under armen og pipa i munnen. Høyt oppe i lia ligger den lille gården.

english.caption: It’s always better to have a rooster than a goose, thought Gudbrand.
english.alt: Gudbrand strolls happily along a dusty road with a brown rooster under his arm and his pipe in his mouth. High up on the hillside lies his little farm.

illustrations.prompt: On a bright morning, Gudbrand sets off down the steep, zigzagging path from the Hillside Farm, leading the black cow with the white face on a rope, his pipe in the corner of his mouth, and looks back with a cheerful wave. At the dusky-blue cottage door, the Wife waves him off with a big smile, the three children crowding round her skirts. Far below, the valley road winds away towards a small town.

simplified.anchor: Det syntes Gudbrand var både riktig og fornuftig sagt.
simplified.caption: Han tok kua med én gang og gikk til byen for å selge henne.
simplified.alt: Gudbrand går nedover den bratte stien med kua i et tau og vinker. Oppe ved døra står kona og de tre ungene og vinker tilbake. Langt nede i dalen ligger byen.

english.anchor: Gudbrand thought that was both right and sensible.
english.caption: He took the cow and went straight to town to sell her.
english.alt: Gudbrand walks down the steep path leading the cow on a rope and waves. At the cottage door, his wife and the three children wave back. Far below in the valley lies the town.

illustrations.prompt: On a dusty road between stubble fields and yellowing birches, Gudbrand hands the rope of his black cow with the white face to a lanky horse dealer in a long grey coat and a battered hat, and takes the reins of a sandy-yellow fjord horse in return. The horse stamps, raising a puff of dust, and Gudbrand pats its neck, delighted with himself, while the cow looks back at him over her shoulder.

simplified.anchor: Han hadde ikke gått langt før han møtte en mann som skulle selge en hest.
simplified.caption: Hest er bedre enn ku, tenkte Gudbrand.
simplified.alt: På en støvete vei gir Gudbrand kua til en fremmed mann og tar imot tøylene til en lys fjordhest. Hesten stamper i støvet, og Gudbrand ser svært fornøyd ut.

english.anchor: He hadn’t gone far when he met a man with a horse to sell.
english.caption: A horse is better than a cow, thought Gudbrand.
english.alt: On a dusty road, Gudbrand hands the cow to a stranger and takes the reins of a pale fjord horse. The horse stamps in the dust, and Gudbrand looks very pleased.

illustrations.prompt: Late afternoon by the roadside, with the low sun turning the dust and the stubble fields to gold. Gudbrand sits contentedly on a big stone with his hat pushed back, a round loaf of bread in one hand and a long sausage in the other, his cheeks full and his eyes closed with pleasure. A little way down the road, a farm boy in a blue cap walks off with the cinnamon-brown rooster tucked under his arm.

simplified.anchor: Dyrene ble mindre og mindre, og veien ble lengre og lengre.
simplified.caption: Det er da alltid bedre å berge livet enn å ha hane, tenkte Gudbrand i Lien.
simplified.alt: Gudbrand sitter på en stein ved veien og spiser brød og pølse med lukkede øyne. Litt bortenfor går en gutt av sted med hanen under armen.

english.anchor: The animals kept getting smaller and the road kept getting longer.
english.caption: It’s always better to save your life than to keep a rooster, thought Gudbrand.
english.alt: Gudbrand sits on a stone by the road eating bread and sausage with his eyes closed. A little way off, a boy walks away with the rooster under his arm.

illustrations.prompt: Dusk at the Hillside Farm, with the first stars and a big orange moon rising over the mountains. Gudbrand walks calmly in at the dusky-blue cottage door, dust on his boots, and warm light from the room falls out over the threshold. Beside the door, the Neighbour presses himself flat against the log wall, holding his breath, one hand cupped behind his big ear and a sly, eager look on his face.

simplified.anchor: Gudbrand ble sittende der til kvelden.
simplified.caption: Hundre daler var mye penger, og nabomannen ville ikke gå glipp av et eneste ord.
simplified.alt: Det skumrer. Gudbrand går inn døra, og varmt lys faller ut over terskelen. Ved siden av døra står naboen klistret inntil veggen med hånda bak øret.

english.caption: A hundred dalers was a great deal of money, and the neighbor didn’t mean to miss a single word.
english.alt: It is dusk. Gudbrand goes in at the door, and warm light spills over the threshold. Beside the door, the neighbor presses himself against the wall with a hand behind his ear.

illustrations.prompt: A wide view of the Cottage Room in the evening, lit by the fire and a candle on the table. The Wife claps her hands together in delight, beaming at Gudbrand, and turns to call to the three children sitting at the table. Gudbrand stands just inside the door with his hat in his hands and his pipe gone out, looking a little sheepish.

simplified.caption: «Nei, nei! Det er jo akkurat det jeg ville gjort selv!»
simplified.alt: Kona slår hendene sammen av glede og smiler til Gudbrand. Ved bordet sitter de tre ungene, og Gudbrand står innenfor døra med hatten i hendene.

english.anchor: “Why, that’s exactly what I’d have done myself!” cried his wife.
english.caption: “Why, that’s exactly what I’d have done myself!” cried his wife.
english.alt: The wife claps her hands with delight and beams at Gudbrand. The three children sit at the table, and Gudbrand stands inside the door with his hat in his hands.

illustrations.prompt: A close, warm view across the supper table in the Cottage Room by candlelight. The Wife has sat down beside Gudbrand and pats his arm, her eyes shining with delight. Gudbrand, his hat on the table beside him, looks at her with relief and the beginning of a smile, his pipe in his hand. On the table: wooden bowls of porridge, a round loaf and a jug of milk.

simplified.caption: «Har jeg sau, får jeg ull og klær i huset, og mat også.»
simplified.alt: Kona sitter ved siden av Gudbrand ved kveldsbordet og klapper ham på armen. Gudbrand ser lettet på henne, og hatten ligger på bordet.

english.anchor: “Why, you clever man!” cried his wife.
english.caption: “A sheep gives me wool and clothes for the house, and meat besides.”
english.alt: The wife sits beside Gudbrand at the supper table and pats his arm. Gudbrand looks at her with relief, his hat on the table.

illustrations.prompt: In the Cottage Room, the Wife stands in the middle of the floor laughing, her head thrown back and her elbows flapping like a crowing rooster. Gudbrand, at the end of the table, scratches the back of his neck and peeks up at her. The three children sit at the table bent over their bowls and do not even look up.

simplified.anchor: «Gud vet hvordan du finner på alt sammen!» ropte kona.
simplified.caption: «En hane! Den er like god som et ur på veggen.»
simplified.alt: Kona står midt i stua og ler og flakser med albuene som en hane som galer. Gudbrand klør seg i nakken, og ungene ser ikke engang opp fra bollene sine.

english.anchor: “Heaven knows how you think of it all!” cried his wife.
english.caption: “A rooster! Why, he’s as good as a clock on the wall.”
english.alt: The wife stands in the middle of the room, laughing and flapping her elbows like a crowing rooster. Gudbrand scratches his neck, and the children don’t even look up from their bowls.

illustrations.prompt: Night at the Hillside Farm, seen from the dark yard under the moon and stars. Gudbrand has swung the dusky-blue door wide open, and warm light pours out onto the ground. On the doorstep, the Neighbour is still bent over with his ear exactly where the door had been, caught and gaping. Behind Gudbrand in the bright room, the Wife smiles as sweetly as ever.

simplified.caption: Der sto nabomannen ute i mørket, med øret akkurat der døra hadde vært.
simplified.alt: Gudbrand har slått opp døra, og varmt lys strømmer ut i mørket. Utenfor står naboen bøyd, med øret der døra var, og inne i stua smiler kona.

english.anchor: Then Gudbrand swung the door wide open.
english.caption: There stood the neighbor in the dark, with his ear exactly where the door had been.
english.alt: Gudbrand has flung the door open, and warm light pours out into the dark. Outside, the neighbor stands bent over with his ear where the door had been, and inside, the wife smiles.
